title: Leave a Trace
content:
What problem does this solve?
Python can do work without showing you anything. print() gives you a simple way to see a value or message while the program runs.

Start with the behavior
Python reads these beginner programs from top to bottom. When it reaches print("hello"), it shows hello in the output area. Text inside quotes is text data. A line that starts with # is a note for the person reading the code; Python does not run that note.

Smallest useful shapes
  print("hello")
  print("first")
  print("second")
  # a comment for the reader

Vocabulary after the behavior
A piece of quoted text is a string. print(...) is a function call. What the program shows is output.

When this is useful
Use print() when you need to observe what a program did. Use comments to leave short explanations for a future reader.
concepts: Python runs these simple statements from top to bottom
print() shows a value in the output area
A # comment is for humans and does not run

examples.title: One line
examples.explanation: Python runs the print call and shows hello.

examples.title: Order matters
examples.explanation: The first print runs before the second.

examples.title: Expedition transfer
examples.explanation: The Python behavior is unchanged; only the data is themed.

common_mistakes: Leaving quotes off literal text makes Python treat the word like a name
Expecting a # comment to produce output
Assuming the lines can run in any order

exercises.title: Read one print
hints: Look only at the value inside print(...).
The quotes mark text; the quotes themselves are not part of the normal output.
The single output line is hello.

exercises.title: Change the message
exercises.prompt:
Change the quoted text so the program prints exactly:
ready
hints: Only the message needs to change.
Keep the parentheses and quotes; replace the text inside the quotes.
exercises.success_message: You changed the program's visible output without changing its structure.

exercises.title: Two lines in order
exercises.prompt:
Write two print() calls so the output is exactly:
first
second
hints: Each output line can come from one print() call.
Write the first print before the second because Python runs top to bottom.

exercises.title: Quote the text
exercises.prompt: This is supposed to print SEARCH. Repair the line.
hints: Python is currently treating SEARCH like a name instead of literal text.
exercises.failure_message: The program should treat SEARCH as quoted text and print one line.

exercises.title: Expedition dispatch
exercises.prompt:
Print exactly these three lines:
SEARCH DISPATCH
Expedition: 17
Status: OVERDUE

Include one useful # comment in your code for a future reader.
exercises.reference_solution:
# Search authorization for Expedition 17
print("SEARCH DISPATCH")
print("Expedition: 17")
print("Status: OVERDUE")
hints: Plan one print() call for each required output line.
A comment can sit on its own line and begins with #; it should explain something about the code.
Write the comment, then three print() calls in the same order as the required output.

tests.message: Use at least three print() calls.

exercises.success_message: You produced a small readable dispatch and left a note for the next reader.
